chunks: 2912 - Al-Bazanti narrated from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: You know my occupation. A woman comes to me, and I know her by her Islam, her love for you, and her wilayah to you; she has no mahram.
He said: "If the Muslim woman comes, then carry her, for the believing man is a mahram for the believing woman."
Then he recited this verse: 'And the believing men and the believing women are allies of one another.'

key_terms.بِإِسْلَامِهَا: her being known as a Muslim
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: a person who serves as a lawful protective escort in this context
key_terms.وَوَلَايَتِهَا: her allegiance and wilayah toward the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim woman perform hajj without a mahram according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a Muslim woman traveling for hajj without a mahram, indicating that a believing man may serve in that protective capacity in this context. The Imam عليه السلام supports the ruling by reciting the verse about mutual wilayah among believing men and women, showing a basis of communal protection and solidarity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2912 - Al-Bazanti narrated from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "You know my profession. A woman comes to me, and I know her to be Muslim, to love you, and to hold your guardianship (wilayah), but she has no mahram (close male relative)."
Imam (as) said: "If a Muslim woman comes, then take her, for a believer is a mahram for a believing woman."
He then recited the verse: 'And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another.' (Surah At-Tawbah 9:71).
